title: Psalm 121: The LORD Who Keeps You
summary: A traveler looks up at the hills and asks where help will come from, then answers: from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth. A second voice takes up the answer and turns it into a blessing, promising that the LORD who never sleeps will keep the traveler from stumbling, from the sun by day and the moon by night, and from all evil, on every road out and every road home.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 120
from.text: Psalm 120 opens the Songs of Ascents, a collection of fifteen short psalms (120 to 134) that each carry the heading

line: A traveler looks to the hills and asks where help will come from: from the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth, who never sleeps and keeps his going out and his coming in.
guide: Ask where you look first for help, and look past it to the one who made the hills. Pray it over someone you love as they set out, or over yourself facing a long road. It does not promise that no harm will ever come.

care.text: If harm has come to you or someone you love, it is not because you trusted God too little.

stanzas.title: The pilgrim's question and confession: help from the Maker
Shade by day and by night
Kept from all evil, going and coming, forever

verses.t: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to the hills. From where does my help come?
My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.
He will not allow your foot to slip; your Protector will not slumber.
Behold, the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD is your keeper; the LORD is the shade on your right hand.
The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.
The LORD will guard you from all evil; He will preserve your soul.
The LORD will watch over your coming and going, both now and forevermore.
